title: private-deployments-weekly-2026-06-01
content:
Weekly update: Private Deployments (VPC / on-prem installs) - week ending 2026-06-01

Summary:
- Focus this week: unblock three active customer installs, finalize our VPC peering automation for GCP/AWS, and stabilize on-prem installer for RHEL8 images.
- Overall status: 2 installs GO (green), 3 in progress with customer blockers, 1 escalated (PD-4821).

Completed this week:
- Customer: BrightHealth (on-prem)
  - Completed appliance install validation and KV cache warmup tests.
  - Post-install smoke tests passed (latency/throughput within expected for their 8GPU cluster).
  - Action: onboarding doc shared, next: schedule runbook walkthrough with CS (owner: Claire, due 2026-06-04).

- VPC peering automation (AWS + GCP)
  - Merged IAM role rotation support for peering scripts (PR #312).
  - Added retry/backoff when Terraform apply times out behind aggressive corporate proxies.
  - Deployed to staging; ran 5 test peering configs end-to-end.

- On-prem installer improvements
  - Fixed installer failure on RHEL8 when cert chain includes intermediate CA - root cause: openssl default path mismatch.
  - Updated installer docs and added explicit cert-install step.

In-progress / Blockers (high priority):
- PD-4821 (AcmeBank) - escalated (customer-production connect)
  - Symptom: install stuck at "register-node" step; logs show TLS handshake failures to control plane.
  - Investigation: appears to be a corporate proxy performing TLS MITM and presenting internal CA certs.
  - Mitigation tried: customer uploaded CA bundle, but installer still fails during mutual TLS because client cert not forwarded by proxy.
  - Next steps: schedule live troubleshooting with customer's network/security team and SREs (owner: Ben). Deadline: 2026-06-03.
  - Related artifacts: JIRA PD-4821, Slack thread #acmebank-install.

- PD-4870 (RetailCorp) - VPC peering failing intermittently
  - Symptom: intermittent route propagation in partner VPN leading to packet drops between app subnet and DB subnet.
  - Root cause hypothesis: BGP session flapping due to MTU mismatch on on-prem firewall.
  - Workarounds: we implemented an aggressive retry in the installer to reapply routes; still flaky under heavy load.
  - Action: escalate to infra networking; customer asked for a temporary hosted fallback for critical latency-sensitive traffic (owner: Miguel).

- GovHealth (private cloud) - compliance docs outstanding
  - Compliance/security team requires signed SOC2 addendum and local KMS attestation docs before we can proceed with private deployment.
  - Legal and security have drafted the attestation; waiting on customer procurement to sign (owner: Ravi).

Standup highlights / daily logs:
- 2026-05-26 (Mon)
  - Claire: Validated BrightHealth logs, preparing runbook.
  - Miguel: Working peering retries; found issue with AWS route table propagation delay.
  - Ben: Started deep-dive on AcmeBank TLS errors.

- 2026-05-28 (Wed)
  - Aisha: Coordinated with SRE for remote debug session; booked session with AcmeBank for 2026-06-02 10:00 PST.
  - Ravi: Drafted KMS attestation for GovHealth.
  - Team: Agreed to add explicit network MTU check to installer preflight.

- 2026-05-29 (Thu) - Customer sync (AcmeBank)
  - Attendees: Aisha (eng lead), Ben (SRE), Claire (CS), AcmeBank network lead (L. O'Connell), security lead (M. Patel)
  - Notes:
    - Customer confirmed corporate proxy is doing TLS inspection and will provide proxy config and CA chain by EOD.
    - We requested temporary access to an internal bastion host to run packet captures during the next install attempt.
    - Agreed: we will update installer to support passing client cert via proxy (depends on proxy feature flags).
  - Action items:
    - Customer: provide proxy config + CA bundle (due 2026-06-01).
    - Ben: prepare debug commands and packet-capture playbook (due 2026-06-02).

Meetings / syncs scheduled next week:
- 2026-06-02 10:00 PST - Live debug with AcmeBank (Ben, Aisha, Claire)
- 2026-06-03 14:00 PST - Post-install runbook walkthrough BrightHealth (Claire, CS)
- 2026-06-04 09:00 PST - Engineering triage: peering flaps + MTU check (Miguel, infra-net, SRE)

Risks / escalations:
- Risk: If AcmeBank TLS issues persist beyond 2026-06-03, they will need an interim hosted routing fallback which impacts our SLA and billing model. Sales/customer success already notified and pricing impact under review.
- Risk: Persistent VPC peering flaps could delay RetailCorp go-live by 2-3 weeks if on-prem firewall vendor requires firmware update.

Action items (owners):
- Ben: Prepare packet-capture playbook and debug checklist for TLS proxy installs (due 2026-06-02).
- Miguel: Add MTU preflight check to installer and increase retry backoff for route apply (PR and staging test by 2026-06-03).
- Claire: Schedule BrightHealth runbook walkthrough and publish onboarding doc to Confluence (due 2026-06-03).
- Ravi: Follow up with Legal and GovHealth procurement for signed KMS attestation (due 2026-06-05).
- Aisha: Coordinate hosted fallback pricing proposal with CS/Sales if AcmeBank needs interim solution (due 2026-06-04).

Notes / misc:
- Suggested improvement: add a short network diagnostics bundle to the installer that runs traceroute, MTU, and TLS handshake tests and uploads anonymized results to S3 for faster triage. Miguel will prototype.
- Reminder: update internal runbook for handling TLS-inspecting proxies (link in linked_artifacts).

If anything urgent comes up over the weekend, ping #private-deployments on Slack and DM Aisha.

End of week note: overall progress steady; main blocker is AcmeBank TLS proxy - priority escalation in progress.
